took_what: This session's own AUT-PD-046 cycle (CYC-0040/0041) backfilled AUT-PROP-030's `what` field and surfaced that it documents a REAL, already-measured concurrency bug in claim.py itself — the exact tool every cycle this session used to coordinate: on a rejected push (lost the race), the reset/unstage sequence leaves the claim's edit sitting in the working tree, so the subsequent merge against the refreshed trunk falsely reports a merge conflict that `git merge --abort` then can't even abort (proving it was never a real conflict). A second, related gap: push()/fetch() collapse 'remote unreachable' and 'remote refused' into one boolean, so a network fault burns the retry budget and gets misreported as contention. Claimed cleanly on attempt 1.
